subtitle: Clean state-by-year India crime statistics, every number linked to its source
userSpecifiedSources: National Crime Records Bureau (ncrb.gov.in), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India: Crime in India, Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India, Prison Statistics and additional tables, read from the live site and from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (web.archive.org), including files since removed. Also Bureau of Police Research & Development, National Human Rights Commission, National Commission for Women, National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Narcotics Control Bureau and Ministry of Home Affairs documents. Place-to-state lookup: GeoNames (geonames.org, CC BY 4.0). Collection code and the full list of upstreams: https://github.com/chandranshB/CrimeBase (SOURCES.md).
description:
# India crime data you can trace

Official crime statistics from India's **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**, cleaned into one tidy table and linked to the exact document each number came from, plus classified crime-news metadata. Rebuilt automatically every day.

## Start here
| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `crime_state_year.csv` | **The clean table.** One row per state/UT x year x crime head x measure (cases registered, persons arrested, convicted, victims ...). Only numbers that add up: state rows against NCRB's own all-India figure, or the districts of a state against NCRB's own state total (`source` says which). Duplicates across files collapsed; disagreements flagged in `disputed`. 2001-2022. |
| `crime_india_year.csv` | The same for **all of India**: NCRB's national crime-head tables plus the all-India row of every state table, so 2001-2015 and 2018 onward join up. |
| `documents.csv` | Every source document: title, publisher, original URL, Internet Archive permalink, and how many numbers it gave. Join on `file`. |
| `facts.parquet` | Everything NCRB's Excel tables contain, and its PDF tables whenever their columns add up, one number per row (states, districts, cities, crime heads), with metric, category, year, `qc` flag and full provenance. About 8.7 million rows. |
| `news.parquet`, `news_events.parquet` | Crime stories from Indian news feeds: category, state, district, victim group, stage of the case, link, one-line summary; and one row per distinct event. |
| `facts_pdf_lowconf.parquet` | PDF figures nothing could check (the table has no total to add up to). Check against the source before use. |
| `ref_states.csv`, `ref_categories.csv` | Code lists. |
| `PROFILE.md`, `DATA_DICTIONARY.md` | Coverage and known gaps (regenerated every run); every column explained. |

The other files (`facts_raw.parquet`, `parse_state.json`, `unmapped_states.csv`, `news_snapshots.txt`, `news_rejected.txt`) are the pipeline's working state; ignore them.
The original PDFs and spreadsheets are in the companion dataset **crimebase-raw**: a row's `file` is `raw-<first character of file>/<file>` there.

## Quick start
```python
import glob, pandas as pd
D = glob.glob('/kaggle/input/**/crime_state_year.csv', recursive=True)[0].rsplit('/', 1)[0]   # the dataset's folder, wherever Kaggle mounts it
p = pd.read_csv(f'{D}/crime_state_year.csv')

# murders registered in India under the IPC, by year
n = pd.read_csv(f'{D}/crime_india_year.csv')
m = n[(n.scope == 'ipc') & (n.crime_head == 'Murder') & (n.metric == 'cases_registered')]
print(m.set_index('year').value)

# where did a number come from?
docs = pd.read_csv(f'{D}/documents.csv')
print(m.merge(docs[['file', 'source_url', 'wayback_url']], on='file').iloc[0])

# state by state, 2015
st = p[(p.scope == 'ipc') & (p.crime_head == 'Murder') & (p.metric == 'cases_registered') & (p.year == 2015)]
print(st.nlargest(5, 'value')[['state', 'value']])

# crime news: distinct events by category
e = pd.read_parquet(f'{D}/news_events.parquet')
print(e.groupby('category').size().sort_values())
```
A worked example is in the notebook **CrimeBase quickstart**.

## Why you can rely on it
* **Sourced**: every row names its document; documents carry the original URL and the Internet Archive permalink of the exact capture.
* **Checked**: state values are summed and compared with NCRB's own all-India row, and the districts of each state with NCRB's own state total (`qc` in `facts.parquet`; only `sum_ok` and `block_ok` rows enter the state table). Where two NCRB tables report the same figure they agree (98% of 29,000 overlapping figures).
* **Honest**: conflicting values are kept and flagged, years are never guessed from ranges (when NCRB copies last year's title into a new file, the file name's year wins), and inferred fields (metric, category) are labelled as inferred.
* **No redundancy**: identical files are stored once; identical facts collapse to one row.
* **Private by design**: no FIR or victim-level data; headlines and summaries of sexual-offence and child-victim stories are withheld.

## Know the limits
Reported crime is not actual crime: registration practices differ by state and year, and the move from IPC to BNS (2024 onward) needs care across years. Coverage follows what NCRB published; PDF-only tables are read from their text and kept only when their columns add up (see `PROFILE.md` for the exact map of what each year holds). News is a sample of public feeds, not a census. `scope` matters: the same head (rape, murder) appears in several table families that overlap, so never add across scopes.

## Updates and credit
Refreshed daily by an open-source pipeline (AGPL-3.0): https://github.com/chandranshB/CrimeBase. Maintained by Chandransh. If this helps your work, a citation is appreciated: *Chandransh, CrimeBase: source-cited India crime data (Kaggle / GitHub, chandranshB/CrimeBase).* Corrections are welcome on GitHub. Government data is published under India's open data policy. Place names are resolved to states with GeoNames data (CC BY 4.0), so city and district rows and news headlines carry a state even when none is printed; such rows are marked (state_inferred, state_basis).

fields.name: state_code
fields.description: ISO 3166-2:IN code of the state or union territory (MH, DL, KL ...); see ref_states.csv.

fields.name: state
fields.description: State / UT name (current names; Orissa = Odisha etc.).

fields.name: year
fields.description: Calendar year the number refers to.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Which NCRB table family the number comes from: ipc, sll, women, children, scheduled_castes, scheduled_tribes, senior_citizens, juveniles, cyber. The same head appears in several families (rape under ipc and women), so keep scope in any filter.

fields.name: crime_head
fields.description: Crime head exactly as the table prints it, parent heads first, joined by ' | ' (e.g. 'Murder (Sec.302 IPC) | A) Murder with Rape/POCSO').

fields.name: crime_category
fields.description: Canonical category of the head (see ref_categories.csv); all_crimes = a grand total, other = no rule matched. Inferred from the head text.

fields.name: metric
fields.description: What the number counts: cases_registered, cases_chargesheeted, cases_convicted, persons_arrested, persons_chargesheeted, persons_convicted or victims.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The number as published.

fields.name: disputed
fields.description: True if another file reports a different value for the same state, year, scope, head and metric; the value shown is the one most tables agree on.

fields.name: source
fields.description: state_table = a row of NCRB's state-wise table (the states add up to NCRB's all-India row); district_total = NCRB's own state Total row of a district-wise table (the districts add up to it). The district tables are how 2016-2020 get states.

fields.name: table_id
fields.description: NCRB's own table number (TABLE 3A.2 ...); empty for older files that carry none.

fields.name: file
